items.title: L'Ue richiama l'Italia sul tetto agli stranieri a scuola. Valditara: 'Andiamo avanti, nessuna discriminazione'
items.summary: La Commissione: 'Seguiamo gli sviluppi del decreto legge italiano'. La replica del ministro
items.content:
La Commissione Ue "segue attentamente" gli sviluppi legislativi del decreto legge sulla scuola adottato in Italia . Lo ha riferito la vicepresidente dell'esecutivo Ue, Roxana Mînzatu, in risposta a un'interrogazione del Pd all'Eurocamera, ricordando che i trattati Ue vietano ogni forma di "discriminazione in base alla nazionalità", sia "diretta" che "indiretta".

La discriminazione per nazionalità è "ammessa dal diritto Ue" solo "in presenza di una deroga prevista dal trattato", ad esempio per "motivi di ordine pubblico, pubblica sicurezza o sanità pubblica". In ogni caso, tali deroghe devono essere interpretate "restrittivamente".

"Il problema non esiste. Il governo va avanti senza esitazioni", dice il ministro dell'Istruzione e del Merito Giuseppe Valditara replicando a Bruxelles. "Premesso che l'istruzione non è una norma di competenza esclusiva della Ue, come indicano tutti i report internazionali - aggiunge - la norma è a favore della integrazione: si riferisce a quegli stranieri che non conoscano la lingua e dunque non realizza alcuna discriminazione. Nella gran parte dei paesi europei gli studenti stranieri di primo arrivo sono addirittura inseriti in classi separate".

items.title: Re Carlo al Commonwealth: 'Orrore e vergogna per lo schiavismo'
items.summary: Il sovrano esprime rammarico 'per le mostruose ingiustizie' dell'Impero Britannico
items.content:
Re Carlo III ha espresso oggi "orrore" e "vergogna" per le colpe storiche del traffico di schiavi, legate al passato coloniale del defunto Impero Britannico, parlando a St John's, capitale di Antigua e Barbuda, all'apertura del vertice biennale dei leader del Commonwealth.

Il sovrano, presidente d'onore dell'organismo, non ha rivolto scuse formali alle ex colonie, ma vi ha fatto cenno a titolo personale evocando il suo dolore e rammarico.

Nel suo discorso d'inaugurazione del summit, alla presenza dei leader di una organizzazione nata proprio dalle ceneri dell'ex Impero e che comprende oggi 56 Stati, re Carlo ha definito lo schiavismo transatlantico alimentato dalle potenze coloniali europee fra Africa, Caraibi e America "una mostruosa ingiustizia". "Questo capitolo vergognoso della storia - ha proseguito - è uno di quelli che riempiono il mio cuore di orrore e la mia anima di un dolore personale profondo".

Attorno al tavolo del vertice, il sovrano di casa Windsor era affiancato dalla nuova segretaria generale del Commonwealth, l'ex diplomatica ghanese Shirley Botchwey, che nei giorni scorsi ha unito la sua voce a quella dei leaderi (caraibici in primis) che sollecitano al monarca e al governo di Londra un percorso verso un atto solenne di scuse ufficiali per lo schiavismo.

Atto su cui il neopremier laburista britannico Andy Burnham - giunto ieri a St John's con gli altri capi di Stato e di governo - ha aperto spiragli inediti di recente, rispetto a tutti i suoi predecessori, sfidando le polemiche interne e mettendo sul piatto anche un alleggerimento del debito e un incremento degli aiuti ai partner del Commowealth interessati; ma tornando a escludere le richieste di "riparazioni finanziarie" dirette come "una risposta sbagliata". Richiesta che invece il primo ministro di Antigua e Barbuda, Gaston Browne, introducendo oggi re Carlo, ha in sostanza rilanciato, auspicando che alle parole seguano passi concreti del Regno Unito in direzione di "una giustizia riparatrice".

items.title: Italjet a EICMA 2026: Roadster 400 a 7.995 euro e tutte le novità Dragster
items.summary: Italjet presenta a EICMA 2026 il Roadster 400 di serie, con motore da 42 CV e prezzo di 7.995 euro. Novità anche per Dragster, accessori GIVI e Moto2
items.content:
Italjet arriva a EICMA 2026 con una gamma che continua a distinguersi per soluzioni tecniche originali e un design immediatamente riconoscibile. Il costruttore bolognese, fondato nel 1959 da Leopoldo Tartarini, porta al Salone di Milano le nuove colorazioni del Roadster 400, conferma l'espansione della famiglia Dragster e annuncia importanti sviluppi commerciali e sportivi.L'attenzione si concentra soprattutto sul Roadster, atteso in produzione nella primavera del 2027 con un prezzo già definito. Accanto a questo modello trovano spazio i Dragster 300, 459 SmartShift e 700 Twin, mentre una nuova collaborazione con GIVI introduce soluzioni dedicate al trasporto dei bagagli. Il marchio prepara inoltre il debutto negli Stati Uniti e rafforza il proprio impegno nelle competizioni.

Roadster 400, quattro colori e prezzo di 7.995 euro

Presentato per la prima volta a EICMA 2025, il Roadster 400 si prepara alla commercializzazione dopo il successo della Founders Edition. La serie inaugurale, limitata a 777 esemplari numerati nelle colorazioni Matt Anthracite e British Racing Green, è andata esaurita in appena 46 minuti. A Milano debutta ora la versione destinata alla produzione regolare.Le nuove tinte disponibili saranno Nero Stellato, Avorio, Verde Menta e Rosso Bologna. La carrozzeria conserva un'impostazione che valorizza la meccanica a vista, con telaio a traliccio in acciaio e componenti strutturali integrati nel disegno complessivo, mentre il motore monocilindrico da 400 cc, raffreddato a liquido, sviluppa 42 CV e 41,2 Nm di coppia, mentre il peso a secco dichiarato è di 151 kg.Tra le caratteristiche tecniche spicca il sistema brevettato DLAS, uno sterzo articolato progettato per combinare precisione e comfort. La dotazione invece comprende freni Brembo con ABS, controllo di trazione e strumentazione TFT, mentre le sospensioni Öhlins e lo scarico AkrapoviÄ saranno disponibili come optional. La produzione partirà nella primavera 2027, con un prezzo di 7.995 euro, IVA inclusa e franco concessionario.

Italjet Dragster 300, 459 SmartShift e 700 Twin

La famiglia Dragster continua a rappresentare il versante più sportivo dell'offerta Italjet. Il Dragster 300 conserva il caratteristico telaio a traliccio esposto e una carrozzeria compatta, con un'impostazione che richiama direttamente il mondo delle competizioni.[gallery ids="293746,293747,293748,293749,293750,293751,293752,293753,293754,293755"]Il modello viene utilizzato dal 2025 nella Malossi Racing Academy, iniziativa dedicata alla formazione dei giovani piloti e allo sviluppo tecnico attraverso l'attività in pista. Il programma era stato avviato nel 2023 con il Dragster 200, prima del passaggio alla cilindrata superiore.La gamma comprende inoltre il Dragster 459 SmartShift, già distribuito in diversi mercati internazionali, e il Dragster 700 Twin, modello che combina caratteristiche tipiche degli scooter con un'architettura vicina a quella motociclistica. Insieme alle versioni 125 e 200, queste proposte completano una famiglia articolata su differenti cilindrate.

Accessori GIVI, nuovi mercati e collaborazione con Gresini Racing

Tra le novità di EICMA figura l'accordo con GIVI, che ha sviluppato nuove soluzioni per il trasporto dei bagagli destinate ai Dragster 300, 459 e 700 Twin. Gli accessori sono studiati per integrarsi con le linee dei modelli senza modificarne radicalmente l'impostazione estetica.Sul piano commerciale, Italjet è presente in oltre 50 Paesi e dispone di 40 concessionari ufficiali in Italia. Per il 2027 è previsto l'ingresso negli Stati Uniti, mentre il debutto ufficiale in India avverrà durante l'India Bike Week del 4 e 5 dicembre 2026, grazie alla collaborazione con Motohaus India.Prosegue infine l'impegno sportivo. Italjet conferma la partnership con Gresini Racing in Moto2 per il 2027, terza stagione consecutiva come title sponsor e quarta di collaborazione complessiva. Il costruttore continuerà anche il programma con Malossi, affiancando all'espansione commerciale lo sviluppo delle attività agonistiche.

items.title: Botteghe Oscure, da sede del Pci a hotel a 5 stelle
items.summary: Dormire nelle stanze dove lavorarono Berlinguer e i dirigenti del partito, tra arte e vista sulla Città Eterna
items.content:
Il Bottegone, storica sede del Partito Comunista a Roma, in via delle Botteghe Oscure, comprato da Palmiro Togliatti per 30 milioni di lire, diventa un hotel di lusso. La notizia della vendita del palazzo era nota, ora è stato inaugurato Thompson Rome, l'hotel a 5 stelle con 69 camere e terrazza panoramica tra arte, design e vista sulla Città Eterna, nel palazzo anni Quaranta che ha visto al lavoro i dirigenti del partito comunista, in primis Enrico Berlinguer che salutò la folla affacciandosi al balcone dopo il risultato elettorale del 1975. Gli uffici e alcune sale dove si discuteva sono state sono state riconvertite.

E' rimasto l’ingresso monumentale, con la scultura Parete di Misure di Giò Pomodoro, alcuni simboli storici del movimento comunista e un busto di Antonio Gramsci

Il palazzo di 8 mila metri quadrati si trova a pochi passi da Piazza Venezia e a breve distanza a piedi dal Foro Romano, dal Pantheon e dal Colosseo. Nel corso della ristrutturazione sono stati restaurati gli elementi architettonici originali, tra cui una scenografica scala in marmo.

I lavori hanno inoltre riportato alla luce una parete scultorea e una pavimentazione intarsiata di Pomodoro. Entrambe le opere sono state conservate e hanno ritrovato un ruolo negli spazi dell’hotel che sorge nei pressi dell’antica Crypta Balbi, testimonianza della stratificazione urbana di Roma, in una zona che nei secoli ha preso forma grazie al passaggio e agli scambi di mercanti, pellegrini, artisti, studiosi e viaggiatori provenienti da tutta l’area mediterranea e dall’Europa.

La collezione custodita nell’hotel comprende opere di artisti legati alla Scuola Romana e alla Scuola di Piazza del Popolo, accanto a lavori contemporanei che riflettono la storica apertura culturale di Roma e le influenze internazionali che l’hanno attraversata. Tra gli artisti presenti figurano Francesco Del Drago, Giangaetano Patanè e Guido Strazza.

items.title: Casio CT-FS1: la tastiera intelligente che corregge le note
items.summary: La nuova Casio CT-FS1 adatta automaticamente le note alla musica grazie a Feel Sync.
items.content:
E se fosse possibile suonare una canzone senza preoccuparsi delle note sbagliate? Casio CT-FS1 promette davvero di poterlo fare, e parliamo di una nuova tastiera elettronica che sfrutta una tecnologia chiamata Feel Sync per adattare automaticamente ciò che viene suonato alla musica in riproduzione. Normalmente parliamo di questo brand in relazione agli orologi digitali, ritornati in voga in questi anni, ma stavolta ci ha incuriosito parecchio questa nuova creazione pensata per coadiuvare i musicisti, ma cerchiamo di capire come funziona, perché è davvero particolare.

Attraverso un'applicazione dedicata, l'utente può caricare una canzone presente sul proprio smartphone o tablet. A quel punto il software analizza la struttura musicale del brano, riconoscendone gli accordi e le variazioni armoniche, e così la tastiera è in grado di modificare le note prodotte affinché risultino coerenti con l'accompagnamento.

In pratica, anche premendo tasti casualmente è possibile ottenere un risultato musicalmente armonioso. Questo non significa che la tastiera insegni automaticamente a suonare, ma permette di concentrarsi su altri aspetti importanti, come ritmo, espressione e coordinazione.

items.title: Bear turns 10, and it still feels like day one
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.bear.app/2026/11/bear-turns-10-and-it-still-feels-like-day-one/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50353383 Points: 34 # Comments: 19
items.content:
Back in 2013, three friends who loved Apple and design couldn’t find a notes app they liked, so they built their own. That side project became Bear. It arrived on the App Store in November 2016, and within a year it had been named Mac App of the Year and won an Apple Design Award . This November, the little Bear turns 10 . Today it helps millions of people around the world capture their ideas and organize their lives every day, and we’ve felt so much love and support from all of you along the way.

We couldn’t find a notes app that fit how we write, so we started building our own.

We built it in our spare time. Our day job back then was building apps and websites for clients.

We start rewriting Bear’s editor from scratch, code name “Panda”.

Your feedback showed us where the original Bear was hitting its limits. Six months in, we realized we needed our own Markdown parser too, so we started over. Again.

Bear 2 launches with an all-new editor and 20+ new features.

The full release of Bear Web is almost here, and we have more features brewing in house…

Over the years, one thing we hear again and again is that Bear just feels good to use. So for this special occasion, we want to share the principles behind every design decision we make. Along the way you’ll find some tiny details we’ve hidden all over the app (you may be using a few right now without knowing it), a peek at an idea that never shipped, and some brand new Bear swag. Grab a slice of cake and come on in!

Every change in Bear goes through a long journey from first idea to final release. Big or small, visible or under the hood, they all follow the same two principles: Bear should be delightful to use, and safe to trust.

We want you to feel delighted every time you open Bear. In practice, that comes down to three things.

Simple. No sign up, no tutorial. Just open a note and write. Bear has grown much more powerful over the years, but all of that power waits quietly underneath and never gets in your way.

💡 Did you know? To make sure Bear stays easy to use, we always ask our parents to test it first!

Natural. We believe the best tools disappear while you use them. So we put a lot of effort into making things work exactly the way you expect, and you’ll find these quality of life touches all over the app.

Take moving lines around. Press ⌘⌥ with the up or down arrow to move the current line, which is perfect for rearranging your writing. Bear understands what you’re moving and where it’s going, so it won’t break apart a list or a table along the way. It’s one of those things that feels so obvious you’d never guess someone had to design it.

Rewarding to explore. Bear has a lot of depth, but we don’t believe in pushing everything to your face to promote it because we don’t know when or if you will need them. Many of our favorite user stories start with a happy little accident. Resize an image from its corner, and it snaps to line up with the images around it; swipe left on a note on iOS, and the Info Panel slides into view. We love those “Oh wow, I didn’t expect that to work!” moments. They’re a big part of why we sign off every post with “ Happy writing !”

💡 Did you know? Some of our favorite details are so small that you may be using them without ever noticing. Here are a few to try: ✍️ Typing in bold or italic? Press Return or the same shortcut again to step right out of the style. ⌨️ Press ⌘A inside a code block to select just the code. Press it again to select the whole note. 🖱️ Select some text and type ( , [ , " or ` . Bear wraps your selection instead of replacing it. 🔗 Select some text and paste a URL. The text becomes a link.

You can’t feel truly comfortable in a space you don’t trust. Your notes hold your ideas, your plans, and sometimes things you’d never share with anyone. That’s why safety has shaped Bear’s most fundamental choices from the very start.

Private. We have no servers holding your notes, and we never see what you write. We also don’t build Bear on top of third party APIs, plugins, or outside services we can’t control. If one of them changed its rules, shut down, or simply stopped working, you would be the one paying the price. So we build what matters ourselves, and Bear keeps working the way you expect.

💡 Did you know? We collaborated with Cossack Labs for note encryption to ensure a reliable and smooth experience. Even if your iCloud account were ever hacked, you can rest assured your encrypted notes stay unreadable.

Keeping a note taking app private and standard wasn’t a revolutionary idea in 2016 when we first launched Bear, but today, it kind of is. And we are glad we stick to what we believe since day 1. The world is changing and we don’t know where it leads us to, but we know your notes are safe with us and you have full control of them anytime, anywhere.

Every design in Bear starts with a problem: a feature people need, something that’s broken, or simply something we don’t like. From there, we are on a journey of problem solving.

That usually means a designer and a developer pairing up for a week or two, then bringing something working to the whole team. Then the real fun begins. Matteo, one of our cofounders, describes fun as “clashing heads with wonderful people to make great things.” Everyone in the team gets to express their opinions no matter what title they have. As a matter of fact, job titles mean nothing to us as you can see on our website .

The feedback discussion can be brutal. “No” is a very welcome answer here, with one house rule: you have to give a reason . Wall of text and hour long slack huddles come and go, then the paring up buddies return to the improvement part and provide a second round, a third round, until we are all happy with it. There are lucky days that some ideas get a big yes on the first try. Others spark weeks and months of debate and never ship at all. We’d rather be a little stubborn about what feels like Bear than chase every trend.

💡 Did you know? Back in 2022, we had the idea to create a fourth column for the info panel, TOC, and Backlinks in Bear 2 update. The concept was discussed internally and also shared with on our forum , but at the end we were not convinced by the design at practical level, and thus the feature was never born in Bear 2.

Over the years, Bear has grown up much bigger than we expected with millions of users enjoying Bear everyday. We’ve seen so many different ways of using Bear: prepare teaching materials in school, work as their second brain, or just write grocery lists (yes, that’s our parents!). 10 years is a huge milestone for us and we want to say a huge thank you to everyone no matter if you have been here since day 1 with us, or just downloaded Bear two minutes ago.

We won’t hand you a flashy roadmap, but here’s what we can say for sure. Bear Web is almost ready for its full release, and we’re also working on note versioning and some other top secret things. Beyond that, we’ll keep doing what we’ve done for ten years: working our best to provide you a comfortable, private space to create beautiful notes.

Meet Kumagotchi 1 , a cute pixel bear who lives in a widget on your Home Screen and keeps you company while you write. Its status quietly follows how you use Bear: it strolls around the meadow when you’ve opened Bear recently, scribbles in its own little notebook while you write, watches the clouds while you read, and takes a nap in the grass when you’ve been away for a while. It’s as old as your very first note, and its weight grows with every note you write.

What’s a birthday without a little dress up? We’ve crafted six new app icons 2 for the occasion: a special 10th anniversary icon, Bear with Birdie, a golden Bear, a peeking Bear, and two classic pixel Bears. We hope they bring a bit of fun to your Home Screen, and a gentle reminder to enjoy the little things in life.

Yes, they are finally here! Many of you have been asking for Bear merch and we have been secretly working on them! Our 10th anniversary merch features pixel art of a classic Macintosh with the Bear logo glowing on its screen and our little Birdie perched on top, a nod to where it all began. Check our merch page below to grab your Bear swag!

Thank you for being part of the story, whether you’ve been here since day one or found Bear last week. We’d love to hear about your favorite hidden detail, or one you just discovered in this post. Come say happy birthday to us on our Community Forum , Reddit , X (Twitter) , Bluesky , or directly at bear@shinyfrog.net .

items.title: Study estimates 75% of NFL players who died over 15-year span had CTE
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.nbcnews.com/health/health-news/study-estimates-75-nfl-players-died-15-year-span-may-cte-rcna605975 Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50353335 Points: 82 # Comments: 41
items.content:
An estimated 75% of professional football players who died over a 15-year span had signs of chronic traumatic encephalopathy, or CTE, a study published Wednesday found.

It’s the highest estimate to date. Most recently, a study published in August by the same group estimated that one-quarter of NFL players who died in a five-year span had CTE. The new study, published in JAMA Network Open , put the figure at three times higher.

Not all people with signs of CTE in the brain go on to experience cognitive decline or dementia, and some people may never experience symptoms at all. A smaller proportion of the former players in the analysis were estimated to have dementia, about 27%, the study found.

The results were surprising, said study leader Yorghos Tripodis, the director of statistics and data management at the Boston University Alzheimer’s Disease and CTE Center. Boston University houses the UNITE Brain Bank , which studies the effects of repetitive head trauma in donated brains, including the brains of athletes, military personnel and others.

“I had to double-check the numbers,” Tripodis said. Still, he said, the number is a best guess. “Right now we don’t know how to diagnose CTE when people are alive, so we are trying to estimate.”

In an emailed statement, an NFL spokesperson said, in part, that the league “continuously strives to make the game of football safer, including by implementing strategies to reduce concussions and head impacts.”

When a person’s head jolts during an impact, the brain — which is suspended in fluid inside the skull — can slam into the skull or twist, said Dr. Julian Bailes, chair of the neurosurgery department at Endeavor Health in the Chicago area. Each blow is an opportunity for proteins called tau to build up in the brain.

“If that happens over and over again, that damage accrues,” said Bailes, who wasn’t involved with the new research.

The disease can affect parts of the brain involved with regulating behavior and emotions , which can lead to memory loss, depression, violent mood swings and other symptoms. Those symptoms can also be linked to other illnesses.

Although CTE can cause symptoms similar to those of other neurodegenerative diseases, such as dementia and Parkinson’s disease, the signature it leaves on the brain is unique, Bailes said.

One huge hurdle in studying the prevalence of CTE is that the microscopic changes don’t show up on brain scans. That means the condition can be diagnosed only during an autopsy.

Past research has been criticized for bias, since people with cognitive decline and their families are much likelier to either donate their brains to brain banks after they die or ask for autopsies — a previous study by Boston University researchers found that 99% of the brains donated to research by former NFL players had signs of CTE.

In the new study, Tripodis and his team tried to remove as much of that bias as possible to determine a more accurate estimate of CTE rates in former NFL players. They combined data from the UNITE Brain Bank with national death records of other former NFL players who died from 2008 to 2023.

In total, the researchers looked at data from 396 donated brains, plus information from 1,966 other deceased former NFL players. They factored in the ages of death along with estimated rates of mild cognitive impairment and dementia in former NFL players older than 50.

About 93% of the donated brains had signs of CTE, which shows up as structural damage in the brain. The research team calculated that the families of players with symptoms of cognitive decline were about five times likelier to donate brains than the families of players without symptoms and then performed a statistical analysis to correct for that bias.

From there, they estimated that among the roughly 2,360 former players who died during the 15-year time frame, about 1,760, or nearly 75%, had CTE. In comparison, only about 1% of brains donated to banks in the U.S., Austria and Brazil have signs of the disease, the researchers said.

But plenty of people with signs of CTE never develop symptoms, Tripodis said.

The researchers estimated that 27% of the 2,360 players studied had dementia.

The dementia “can be from all causes,” Tripodis said. “But it is very likely that in this specific population that CTE is causing dementia.”

Until doctors figure out a way to diagnose CTE while people are still alive, any studies quantifying how many people have the condition will be estimates, said Dr. Jim Kelly, a professor emeritus of neurology at the University of Colorado Anschutz.

“These are all estimates. They had no autopsies on five times as many players who died as they did have autopsies for,” said Kelly, who wasn’t involved in the research.

Some of the autopsies may also have revealed just one or a couple of lesions associated with CTE, “and it seems unlikely that that would lead to anything in terms of a behavior change or dementia,” he said.

Those are difficult studies to do, Bailes agreed. They seek to determine “how many people out there have a condition when not all of them are symptomatic,” he said, adding that the findings are a call for more research into diagnosing CTE in people who are still living.

“If you can’t tell if someone has a certain disease until they’re dead, you really can’t help them,” he said.

In the meantime, prevention is key, Tripodis said: “If you reduce the number of brain injuries, brain impacts, you substantially decrease the risk.”

The NFL has already implemented measures to try to reduce the number of high-impact hits players face. They include redesigned helmets — such as the Guardian Cap — and the dynamic kickoff rule , which leads to lower collision speeds.

Kaitlin Sullivan is a contributor for NBCNews.com who has worked with NBC News Investigations. She reports on health, science and the environment and is a graduate of the Craig Newmark Graduate School of Journalism at City University of New York.

items.title: Zontes 853R, la naked da 148 CV debutta a EICMA 2026: prestazioni da superbike
items.summary: Zontes alza l'asticella a EICMA con la nuova 853R: 148 CV, ciclistica raffinata e componentistica di primo piano per sfidare le maxi-naked europee
items.content:
Zontes volta pagina e punta dritto al segmento delle maxi-naked sportive. Archiviata la piattaforma tricilindrica 703, la Casa cinese ha scelto il palcoscenico di EICMA 2026 per svelare la nuova Zontes 853R, una moto che alza nettamente l'asticella sia per il design aggressivo sia per una scheda tecnica che guarda senza timori alle concorrenti più blasonate.

Un tre cilindri da 148 cavalli

Il cuore del progetto è il propulsore tricilindrico di seconda generazione, portato a una cilindrata di 847 cc. I numeri dichiarati raccontano un'indole decisamente spinta:
  • potenza massima: 148 CV;
  • coppia: 90 Nm a 13.000 giri/min di regime massimo;
  • prestazioni dichiarate: 0-100 km/h in 2,8 secondi e una velocità massima di circa 280 km/h.
Valori ambiziosi, chiaramente sulla carta, che andranno verificati sul campo non appena la moto sarà disponibile per un test.

Telaio da 10 chili e freni Brembo Stylema

[gallery ids="293732,293735,293733,293734,293736,293737"]Per gestire la nuova cavalleria, Zontes ha riprogettato il telaio in alluminio (principale e telaietto pesano complessivamente appena 10 kg) per fermare l'ago della bilancia a 183 kg a secco.Il livello della componentistica è notevole per una moto di questa provenienza:
  • sospensioni Kayaba completamente regolabili, con forcella da 43 mm dotata di trattamento antiattrito DLC;
  • forcellone monobraccio in alluminio al posteriore;
  • impianto frenante di primo piano: pinze anteriori Brembo Stylema, pompa radiale Brembo PR16 e dischi flottanti da 310 mm.

Elettronica di bordo e tecnologia NFC

La gestione della potenza è affidata a una piattaforma inerziale IMU a sei assi. Il pacchetto comprende ABS e Traction Control Cornering, controllo dell'impennata su quattro livelli, Launch Control, Quick Shifter bidirezionale e acceleratore Ride-by-Wire.Sul fronte tecnologico spicca la nuova strumentazione digitale integrata con l'app Zontes 2.0 e il sistema Intelligent Control 4.0, che permette tra l'altro di sbloccare e avviare la moto tramite tecnologia NFC utilizzando uno smartphone compatibile, eliminando la chiave tradizionale.

L'unica vera incognita: il prezzo

Le linee sono spigolose, arricchite da un gruppo ottico Full LED, semi-manubri in alluminio e pedane interamente regolabili. Non mancano tocchi raffinati come i componenti in vera fibra di carbonio (alette aerodinamiche, parafanghi e cover serbatoio), il doppio scarico alto e una sella sdoppiata in pelle.Restano da capire i dettagli commerciali. Al momento, infatti, il costruttore non ha comunicato né il listino prezzi per il mercato italiano né la data precisa in cui la 853R arriverà nelle concessionarie, due fattori che saranno determinanti per il suo posizionamento sul mercato.

items.title: Kalshi and its co-founders face felony charges for violating Utah gambling laws
items.summary: Article URL: https://arstechnica.com/tech-policy/2026/10/trump-admin-sues-utah-to-save-kalshi-from-the-states-total-ban-on-gambling/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50353229 Points: 115 # Comments: 68
items.content:
The Trump administration is trying to stop Utah from enforcing its gambling ban against Kalshi, making Utah the 10th state sued by the US government agency that regulates prediction markets.

Meanwhile, Utah Attorney General Derek Brown filed criminal charges in a state court against Kalshi and its founders on Wednesday. The attorney general’s office provided us with court filings listing charges against KalshiEX, LLC , Kalshi co-founder and CEO Tarek Mansour , and Kalshi co-founder and COO Luana Lopes Lara .

The company and two co-founders each face 13 felony charges and one misdemeanor for violating gambling laws. The charges are based on sports bets offered on Kalshi between September 13 and September 24. “The state did not issue arrest warrants for Monsour and Lopes Lara. Instead, they have been issued summons to respond to the charges in Third District Court in Salt Lake County,” The Salt Lake Tribune wrote .

The Utah News Dispatch quoted a Kalshi statement vowing to fight the charges. “This is a crazy overreach; Utah is clearly playing politics. We look forward to putting a stop to this in court, just like we did in Arizona,” the statement said, referring to similar charges the company beat in Arizona in May.

Utah, which prohibits gambling, filed a civil lawsuit against Kalshi in a state court last week. Utah’s lawsuit seeks an order prohibiting Kalshi from offering bets on sports, elections, politics, and other events.

“Kalshi runs an online casino in Utah and calls it a prediction market. That violates Utah law,” Utah Attorney General Derek Brown, a Republican, said last week. “Not only do our state laws ban gambling but Utah is one of only two states where gambling is also prohibited under the state constitution. For 130 years, Utah has been clear: gambling has no place here, and we will enforce our laws.”

Utah already defeated Kalshi in federal court after the prediction market filed a preemptive lawsuit that sought to prevent the state from enforcing its gambling laws. Now that Utah is moving ahead in its attempt to shut down Kalshi, it must defend against a lawsuit filed by the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC).

The CFTC “has filed a lawsuit against Utah to block the state’s efforts to shut down CFTC-registered contract markets using state laws,” the commission said on Tuesday . “The lawsuit follows Utah’s decision to file civil enforcement actions in state court against CFTC-regulated markets and other businesses. Utah’s effort to restrict the functioning of CFTC-registered exchanges obstructs Congress’s decision to federally preempt state law.”

If Utah can shut down Kalshi, that could spell trouble for Kalshi’s chief prediction-market rival, Polymarket, and for sports betting sites like DraftKings and FanDuel. DraftKings and FanDuel advertise availability in all US states via a mix of products , including prediction-market platforms in states like Utah. Both are registered with the CFTC.

The Utah attorney general’s office declined to comment today on the CFTC lawsuit. The CFTC previously filed lawsuits against Arizona, Connecticut, Illinois, Kentucky, Minnesota, New Mexico, New York, Rhode Island, and Wisconsin. The federal agency also filed briefs supporting Kalshi in appeals court cases.

“Utah seeks to shut down prediction markets across a wide variety of markets,” CFTC Chairman Michael Selig said. “Event contracts do not just serve hedging and investment purposes—they also provide the public with information about the outcome of future events. Congress entrusted the CFTC to be the federal regulator with sole responsibility to oversee these markets. As I’ve said before, the CFTC has the expertise and responsibility to defend its exclusive jurisdiction over commodity derivatives, and that’s exactly what we’ll do.”

The US Commodity Exchange Act (CEA) gives the CFTC authority to regulate swaps. The key legal questions being grappled with by courts throughout the US are whether event contracts offered by prediction markets qualify as swaps, and whether the CFTC jurisdiction over swaps preempts states from applying their gambling laws.

The CFTC is suing Utah in the same US district court that previously ruled in Utah’s favor. Kalshi sued Utah in February in an attempt to stop the state from bringing an enforcement action against the prediction market.

In August, US District Judge Robert Shelby granted Utah’s motion for summary judgment and denied Kalshi’s motion for a preliminary injunction. Shelby wrote , “[T]he court concludes the federal law relied upon by Kalshi does not preempt Utah’s ability to enforce its anti-gambling laws.”

Shelby determined the text of US law makes it clear that state regulation is not forbidden. US law states that CFTC jurisdiction does not “supersede or limit the jurisdiction conferred on courts of the United States or any State,” and “explicitly provides for State regulation of its gaming laws in all but a few specified cases,” he wrote.

“Congress is aware that some States permit gambling while others do not, and the CEA explicitly provides for State jurisdiction,” Shelby wrote.

Kalshi is now appealing its loss to the US Court of Appeals for the Tenth Circuit but was unable to obtain an injunction preventing enforcement of the state gambling ban while that litigation continues. On September 8, Tenth Circuit judges denied Kalshi’s emergency motion for an injunction pending appeal. Utah filed its lawsuit seeking a shutdown of Kalshi about six weeks later.

The CFTC lawsuit against Utah makes arguments similar to the ones already rejected by the district court, although some other courts have ruled otherwise.

“Utah is not the first State that has attempted to invade the Commission’s exclusive jurisdiction over swaps,” the CFTC lawsuit said. “Already, several federal courts—including the Third Circuit—have swiftly responded by issuing or affirming temporary restraining orders and preliminary injunctions barring the States from enforcing their gambling laws against CFTC-regulated exchanges that offer sports-related or other event contracts.”

The Third Circuit appeals court ruled that New Jersey cannot regulate sports bets on prediction markets. But Kalshi lost similar cases in the Sixth Circuit and Ninth Circuit in rulings that went in favor of Ohio, Tennessee, and Nevada.

Because circuit appeals courts are divided on the issue, it is likely that the Supreme Court will take up the case and determine whether states can apply their gambling laws to prediction markets. New Jersey petitioned the Supreme Court to resolve the circuit split, and 39 other states and the District of Columbia filed a brief supporting New Jersey’s petition.

This article was originally published on October 28 at 3:30 pm ET and updated on October 29 with information about the felony charges filed against Kalshi and its co-founders .

items.title: Falsi allarmi bomba sui voli in Europa, due anche a Fiumicino
items.summary: Anche a Varsavia, Sofia e Murcia. Controlli negativi, scattate le verifiche sulla sicurezza
items.content:
Falsi allarmi bomba sui cieli europei, due dei quali scattati anche all'aeroporto di Fiumicino, in mattinata, per due voli Ryanair arrivati rispettivamente da Lisbona e Dublino.

A seguito di una segnalazione anonima su un presunto allarme bomba a bordo dei due voli, quello da Lisbona, atterrato intorno alle 9.40, e quello da Dublino atterrato alle 10.44, sono scattati, come da procedura, i controlli di sicurezza su aeromobili, passeggeri e bagagli e le operazioni di bonifica, da parte degli artificieri. Le operazioni delle forze dell'ordine si sono concluse poco dopo mezzogiorno, con esito negativo.

È stata una mail a far scattare l'allarme bomba, poi risultato falso, su due voli Ryanair. Lo si apprende da fonti investigative. Nel messaggio di posta elettronica, che sarebbe arrivata alla società Adr, veniva segnalata la presenza di ordigni sui voli in arrivo da Lisbona e Dublino. Sono scattati i protocolli di sicurezza e, al termine delle bonifiche, l'allarme è rientrato.

"Attivato il protocollo di sicurezza per un allarme bomba su un volo proveniente da Manchester che è atterrato a Murcia ": lo ha segnalato Francisco Lucas, il Delegato del governo spagnolo a Murcia, a sud della Spagna, in un messaggio su X. "I 114 passeggeri e i 7 membri dell'equipaggio sono stati evacuati e sono sottoposti a un controllo di sicurezza", ha informato il prefetto. "In questi momenti, si sta ispezionando l'aereo", ha aggiunto.

Il traffico aereo dell'aeroporto è rimasto per circa due ore interrotto dopo l'allarme, per poi riaprire alle 13. Secondo quanto segnalato dalla Delegazione di Murcia, dopo l'atterraggio del volo, alle 10.30 di questa mattina, e lo sbarco dei 114 passeggeri e di 7 membri dell'equipaggio, sottoposti a controlli di sicurezza, sono state mobilitate squadre di polizia e di artificieri del Tedax della Guardia Civil per la disattivazione di esplosivi. Contemporaneamente erano state limitate le operazioni di decollo e atterraggio, con la chiusura temporanea dello scalo, che ha interessato un solo volo proveniente da Gran Canaria, deviato sull'aeroporto di Alicante, sempre sul versante mediterraneo iberico. Una volta ultimati i controlli di sicurezza, senza che siano state rilevate anomalie, l'aeroporto è stato riaperto per le normali operazioni.

Due aerei passeggeri sono stati ispezionati anche Varsavia , scrive la Bbc. I media locali bulgari riferiscono che anche un aereo proveniente da Israele è atterrato all'aeroporto di Sofia dopo che era stata ricevuta una minaccia di attentato via e-mail. Un volo proveniente da Londra Heathrow ha effettuato un atterraggio non previsto all'aeroporto di Varsavia Modlin, dove è stato ispezionato da esperti. Era diretto verso il principale aeroporto di Varsavia, Chopin, con 181 persone a bordo.

Anche un secondo volo da Copenaghen all'aeroporto Chopin ha ricevuto una minaccia di attentato, secondo quanto riportato dai media danesi. È atterrato regolarmente. Nel frattempo, un aereo della Ryanair proveniente da Manchester ha effettuato un atterraggio di emergenza all'aeroporto di Murcia, nel sud della Spagna, a causa di un'altra minaccia.

A bordo di quel volo c'erano 121 persone, compreso l'equipaggio, secondo quanto riferito da Francisco Lucas, delegato del governo spagnolo nella regione di Murcia. Questi episodi distinti si sono verificati il giorno dopo che un volo della Wizz Air proveniente da Londra Luton ha effettuato un atterraggio di emergenza a Budapest, scortato da un caccia ungherese, a seguito di una minaccia di bomba.

items.title: Vuoi acqua filtrata direttamente dal rubinetto? Questo sistema a osmosi inversa in sconto fa al caso tuo
items.summary: Acqua filtrata direttamente dal rubinetto, senza cloro e impurità: il sistema Mideo a osmosi inversa è ora in offerta a 199 euro. Ha 4 stadi di filtrazione e un display LED che avvisa quando è ora di cambiare i filtri ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Midea MRO2489-600G è un avanzato sistema di filtrazione dell'acqua a osmosi inversa progettato per garantire acqua filtrata direttamente dal tuo rubinetto.

Il sistema utilizza un processo di filtrazione a 4 stadi basato sulla tecnologia a osmosi inversa, con un filtro PAC per il pre-trattamento e una membrana RO per la filtrazione più profonda. È progettato per ridurre la presenza di cloro, sedimenti e altre impurità presenti nell'acqua.

La membrana RO ha una capacità di filtrazione dichiarata fino a 0,0001 micrometri e contribuisce a trattenere particelle microscopiche. Il sistema ha una capacità di produzione di 600 GPD, pari a circa 2.160 litri di acqua filtrata al giorno, e un rapporto tra acqua filtrata e acqua di scarico di 2:1: per ogni due tazze di acqua prodotta, una viene scaricata.

Un display LED a colori segnala lo stato dei filtri e indica quando è necessario sostituirli. La membrana a osmosi inversa ha una durata stimata di uno o due anni, variabile in base alla durezza dell'acqua e alle condizioni di utilizzo.

Il sistema è attualmente disponibile al prezzo scontato di 199,99 € .

items.title: Aumentano del 9% le bollette del gas dei vulnerabili. Arera: 'Pesano le quotazioni'
items.summary: ll prezzo della sola materia prima è di 88,36 euro a megawattora
items.content:
Bolletta del gas più cara ad ottobre per i 2,3 milioni di clienti vulnerabili in Italia per colpa del deciso rialzo delle quotazioni all'ingrosso, sensibili alle tensioni geopolitiche e in particolare alle decisioni dell'Iran sull'apertura o meno dello Stretto di Hormuz.

Influenza rilevata sulla piazza Ttf di Amsterdam, di riferimento per l'Europa, dove il prezzo del metano è andato fin sotto i 90 euro a megawattora (i contratti future a dicembre hanno ceduto il 7,64% a 87,5 euro) per la prima volta dallo scorso 22 ottobre dopo l'annuncio di ieri di Teheran di poter riaprire lo Stretto "entro 48 ore". La quotazione è poi risalita a 90,5 euro al MWh (-4,6%).

Intanto, i depositi di gas nell'Unione europea stanno per affrontare la stagione di riscaldamento 2026-27 con scorte ai livelli più bassi dal 2013, secondo l'Agenzia internazionale dell'energia. Le riserve hanno segnato oggi il primo calo settimanale, scendendo al 74,56% a 844,25 TWh, a causa dei prelievi dovuti al clima più rigido. In Germania sono al 61,05% a 151 TWh e in Italia al 91% a 185,11 TWh, il paese con maggiori scorte disponibili.

La riduzione, ricorda l'Iea, aumenta la dipendenza dalle forniture globali di Gnl per soddisfare i picchi di domanda stagionale e potrebbe rendere l'area molto vulnerabile se il prossimo inverno dovesse essere più freddo del previsto, o in caso di guasti tecnici o altre interruzioni delle forniture. Entro fine marzo 2027, ha calcolato l'agenzia, i livelli di stoccaggio del gas nell'Ue potrebbero scendere sotto il 10% della capacità operativa.

E la velocità con cui il gas può essere prelevato tende a diminuire quando i livelli di riempimento scendono sotto il 30% della capacità operativa. Questo aumenterebbe di molto la necessità di immettere gas negli impianti durante l'estate 2027, prolungando potenzialmente le tensioni sul mercato anche nell'anno successivo, afferma la Iea. "Dalla sola chiusura dello Stretto di Hormuz, le importazioni di combustibili fossili sono costate all'Europa 127 miliardi di euro in più, senza un solo quantitativo aggiuntivo di energia" ha sottolineato la presidente della Commissione europea, Ursula von der Leyen, intervenendo al WinWin Brussels Summit dedicato alle startup. "Quando importiamo petrolio e gas, rischiamo di importare anche gli shock e le crisi che li accompagnano", ha aggiunto.

Tornando all'aumento delle bollette per i vulnerabili in Italia, l'Arera ha comunicato un +9,1% del prezzo del gas ad ottobre con 88,36 euro a Mwh per la sola materia prima gas, che per l'Unione nazionale consumatori è "record storico, il più alto di sempre". Per l'associazione "il Governo Meloni continua a non fare nulla per aiutare gli italiani a pagare queste bollette astronomiche".

L'Unc e il Codacons hanno calcolato 163 euro in più su base annua, nell'ipotesi di prezzi costanti per i prossimi 12 mesi. La spesa totale annua (non, quindi, secondo l'anno scorrevole, ma dal 1 ottobre 2026 al 30 settembre 2027) decolla così a 1.945 euro che, sommati agli 869 euro della luce, determinano una stangata complessiva annua pari a 2.814 euro. Assoutenti parla di "nuova mazzata sui consumatori", "è il sesto aumento consecutivo delle tariffe" e chiede che il "Governo studi sconti sulla tassazione, riducendo subito l'Iva sul gas e tagliando gli oneri di sistema".

items.title: LONGi Hi-MO X12: nuovi pannelli fotovoltaici fino a 690 W
items.summary: LONGi presenta pannelli solari fino a 690 W con nuovi collegamenti elettrici e maggiore affidabilità.
items.content:
Ci sono interessanti novità nel segmento dei Pannelli solari, con un modello che promette fino a 690 W e molti meno guasti rispetto ai modelli attuali. Stiamo parlando dei nuovi Hi-MO X12 di LONGi, presentati durante All Energy Australia 2026.

I moduli offrono un incremento dichiarato fino a 20 W rispetto alle soluzioni tradizionali grazie a una diversa progettazione dei collegamenti elettrici, ma cosa cambia concretamente? Nei pannelli convenzionali, le celle sono collegate attraverso sottili nastri metallici saldati, mentre il nuovo sistema utilizza invece una pellicola posteriore conduttiva, che permette di trasferire l'elettricità eliminando migliaia di potenziali punti critici. Secondo LONGi, questa architettura elimina oltre 15.000 possibili punti di guasto delle saldature per modulo e aumenta dell'85% la sezione disponibile per il passaggio della corrente. Il risultato è un guadagno stimato tra 6 e 8 W.

A questo si aggiunge una disposizione delle celle che riduce gli spazi inutilizzati sulla superficie, recuperando altri 8-12 W. Non solo, il produttore dichiara una riduzione del 90% nella trasmissione del vapore acqueo attraverso la barriera metallica integrata. La gamma comprende moduli da 660 a 690 W per installazioni commerciali e industriali, oltre a versioni più compatte da 495 a 510 W, pensate anche per i tetti residenziali.

items.title: Morto Jesus de Miguel, attaccante del Tenerife, dopo uno scontro in campo
items.summary: All'attaccante del Tenerife fatale l'impatto a centrocampo col portiere di Andorra
items.content:
Tragedia nel calcio spagnolo, sconvolto dalla morte dell'attaccante del Tenerife Jesus de Miguel Alameda. Nell'incontro di serie B contro Andorra, il giocatore é stato travolto a centrocampo dal portiere avversario, Jesus Owono, nazionale della Guinea Equatoriale, uscito precipitosamente dai pali. L'episodio è avvenuto al 97', sul punteggio di 2-2. Owono è stato espulso e l'incontro sospeso.

De Miguel, colpito al petto da una ginocchiata, é rimasto a terra privo di sensi. Le sue condizioni sono apparse subito gravi. Secondo i media locali, ha subito un arresto cardiaco. E' stato rianimato e trasportato nel reparto di terapia intensiva, dove é deceduto qualche ora dopo. Il Tenerife in un primo momento aveva definito le sue condizioni "stabili, seppur gravi". Prima di annunciare la morte, l'ospedale dell'isola delle Canarie aveva reso noto che le sue condizioni erano "peggiorate dal punto di vista neurologico".

De Miguel, 30 anni, militava nel Tenerife da poco più di una stagione: era arrivato nell'estate del 2025 dal Castellón. "Non esistono parole per alleviare il dolore, nulla può lenire questo profondo senso di tristezza. I nostri pensieri vanno alla famiglia, agli amici più cari e ai tifosi del Tenerife, che oggi piangono questa terribile notizia" ha scritto il club delle Canarie sul proprio profilo 'X'. "Sono profondamente addolorato. Riposa in pace, Jesus", é il messaggio sui social di Gerard Piqué, ex difensore del Barcellona e azionista di maggioranza dell'Andorra. Che a sua volta ha espresso le proprie "più sincere condoglianze".

Messaggi di cordoglio sono giunti anche da Real Madrid, Barcellona, Atletico Madrid e da altri club spagnoli, oltre che dalla Federcalcio spagnola, "sconvolta da questa triste notizia". Rafael Nadal, ha parlato di "un dolore immenso" sul suo profilo Instagram. "Il calcio europeo è in lutto", ha fatto sapere l'UEFA, annunciando che questa settimana verrà osservato un minuto di silenzio in tutte le partite delle coppe.

Nel 2001 Serhiy Perkhun, portiere ucraino del CSKA Mosca, 23 anni, perse la vita a causa di un'emorragia cerebrale, 10 giorni dopo uno scontro testa a testa con l'attaccante dell'Anzhi Makhachkala, Budun Budunov. Ancora un estremo difensore vittima di un incidente di gioco, il 14 febbraio del 1965, durante un Sambenedettese-Ascoli. Si chiamava Roberto Strulli, 26 anni, portiere dell'Ascoli, e si accasciò a terra dopo l'impatto con il centravanti avversario, Alfiero Caposciutti. Portato in ospedale, morì poche ore dopo. John Thomson, 22 anni, nel 1931 era il portiere del Celtic Glasgow. Perse la vita durante l'Old Firm contro i Rangers. Thomson si tuffò coraggiosamente sui piedi dell'attaccante avversario Sam English, subendo un impatto devastante tra il ginocchio di quest'ultimo e la propria testa.

items.title: Paywall dei giornali aggirati con il browser Brave: scatta la denuncia
items.summary: Accesso illegale fornito anche alle società di intelligenza artificiale per l'addestramento dei loro modelli
items.content:
Il New York Times e un gruppo di altre pubblicazioni hanno intentato causa contro la società dietro al browser web Brave, accusata di fornire strumenti per bypassare i paywall e quindi accedere agli articoli riservati agli abbonati. Soprattutto, Brave è imputata di scraping illegale per l'addestramento delle AI: secondo la denuncia, avrebbe monetizzato il suo indice di siti web oggetto di scraping fornendo alle aziende di intelligenza artificiale l'accesso a contenuti in tempo reale.

Le aziende AI, quindi, si sarebbero avvalse del Brave Index per addestrare i loro modelli, rispondere a specifiche domande degli utenti o entrambi. Tra le altre, risultano coinvolte Anthropic, Perplexity, Mistral, xAI e Cohere.

"Brave non ha mai chiesto il permesso agli editori di accedere ai loro siti web, tanto meno di copiare il materiale e fornirlo agli utenti o ad altre società di intelligenza artificiale", si legge nella denuncia. Eppure, l'opzione "Paywall blocker" è attiva, funzionante e promossa come la chiave d'accesso a "centinaia di editori top".

items.title: Mining giant joins fight to stop killer toad march across Australia
items.summary: Rio Tinto is jointly funding a A$28m "toad containment zoe" to protect the Pilbara region.
items.content:
Rio Tinto is ploughing millions of dollars into stopping the poisonous cane toad reaching the Pilbara region of western Australia, where the mining giant has a vast iron ore operation.

The firm, alongside Curtin University in Perth and others, will spend A$28m (£14.5m) building a "toad containment zone" to prevent the pest travelling south.

While the cane toad is not a direct threat to Rio Tinto's business, it produces toxins lethal to native wildlife and poses a threat to Pilbara's ecosystem.

Rio Tinto has previously faced criticism for destroying two sacred Aboriginal rock shelters in Pilbara which sat above tonnes of iron ore.

The decision cost the former chief executive his job, provoked a widespread backlash and saw Rio Tinto commit to rebuilding trust with Indigenous communities.

Commenting on the proposed containment zone, Roberta Hunter, a ranger in Australia's Nyangumarta Warrarn Indigenous Protected Area, said: "Cane toads destroy the water and animals.

"When toads come close to our country, we want to be there to stop them because we don't want the country to be destroyed."

The plan is to cut off the toad's water supply by building a barrier across 7,500 sq km (2,895 sq m) of land between the Great Sandy Desert and the Indian Ocean.

In drier months, the cane toad needs water every few days to survive.

If there are no natural water sources, the toad relies on artificial water points normally used for cattle and irrigation.

The funding will be used to stop the toad accessing dams, storage tanks or other ground-level water sources. The five-year project will begin in 2027.

A number of native species are at risk if the toad gets into Pilbara. These include the northern quoll, whose numbers have been decreasing, the goanna lizard and the ghost bat.

The toads were introduced into Australia in 1935 to control beetles within the sugar cane industry.

Since then, they have been on a slow march west across the country's northern landscape, according to the Australian government, travelling between 40 km and 60 km a year.

There are no predators or diseases that control the toads, which defend themselves using poison.

Ben Phillips, a professor at Curtin University, said the toads would reach Pilbara within two decades without action.

He said: "The toad containment zone is a once in a lifetime opportunity to stop one of the world's worst invasive species in its tracks and protect the region's unique wildlife."

items.title: EICMA 2026, debutta la microcar elettrica da 85 km/h: parte da 16.900 euro
items.summary: Eli svela ad EICMA 2026 la nuova ZERO MX L7e da 200 km di autonomia e la serie limitata RACE Edition. Caratteristiche, prestazioni e prezzi per l'Italia.
items.content:
Fino a ieri il marchio americano Eli faceva rima soltanto con quadricicli leggeri. Ma con EICMA 2026 si cambia la marcia. La casa statunitense alza la posta e debutta tra i quadricicli pesanti (L7e) presentando la nuova ZERO MX, affiancata per l'occasione dall'inedita versione speciale ZERO RACE Edition. Due novità chiave che segnano il debutto sul mercato italiano tramite il nuovo importatore e distributore Mobility Trade.

Eli ZERO MX: compatta da città, pronta all'extraurbano

La MX si presenta come l'anello di congiunzione tra la praticità di una microcar e l'usabilità di un'utilitaria. Nonostante le dimensioni restino super compatte, la lunghezza sferra i 2,25 metri esatti dell'intera linea Zero, sottopelle la musica cambia. Si guida dai 16 anni con la patente B1 e spinge fino a 85 km/h grazie a un motore elettrico da 20 kW di potenza di picco.La trazione è posteriore, gestibile con le due opzioni di guida ECO e SPORT. Ma al di là dello scatto, la ZERO MX punta all'agilità pura. Ha un diametro di sterzata stretto (7,2 metri) per infilarsi ovunque e digerisce pendenze fino al 30%. Per il capitolo autonomia, il pacco batterie LFP da 14,4 kWh dichiara fino a 200 km con una sola carica. Il ripristino si fa tramite un caricatore di bordo da 3,3 kW, collegabile a qualsiasi presa di casa o alle classiche colonnine pubbliche in corrente alternata.

Dotazione da "vera" auto: l'abitacolo e la tecnologia

Chi sale a bordo nota subito che l'impostazione va ben oltre lo standard della categoria. Eli ha inserito di serie il climatizzatore con riscaldamento, il tetto panoramico, il sistema keyless per apertura e avvio senza chiave, il servosterzo elettrico e retrocamera con sensori di parcheggio.La sicurezza attiva e passiva conta su quattro freni a disco, sistema ABS e freno di stazionamento elettrico. L'ambiente di guida punta poi al digitale con uno schermo strumentazione dedicato e un display centrale da 10,1 pollici per l'infotainment, completo di Apple CarPlay. A catalogo ci sono quindi quattro tinte: Pearl White, Arctic Silver, Graphite e l'inedita variante Champagne.

Arriva la RACE Edition (e la modalità Turbo)

La fiera milanese fa anche da palcoscenico per la ZERO RACE Edition, una serie speciale a tiratura limitata proposta sia sul modello leggero L6e sia sulla nuova pesante MX L7e.Qui l'impatto visivo fa da padrone. La carrozzeria indossa l'esclusiva tinta Turbo Red con sticker sportivi su cofano, parafanghi e fiancate, completata da uno spoiler posteriore e loghi specifici sui cerchi. Dentro si nota l'ambiente bicolore in microfibra scamosciata Race Red e grigio chiaro, con il logo della serie ricamato sui sedili.E c'è poi una chicca tecnica. La modalità Turbo. Quando la si inserisce, la centralina modifica la curva di risposta del pedale rendendola subito reattiva. Nessun cavallo in più e nessuna velocità massima alterata rispetto ai dati d'omologazione, ma una risposta del gas decisamente più pronta al tocco.

Prezzi, promozione e disponibilità sul mercato italiano

L'intera gamma Eli ZERO si può già ordinare presso la rete di concessionari ufficiali italiani. L'accesso al listino parte da 10.900 euro per la ZERO in versione base (L6e). Per mettersi in garage la nuova ZERO MX L7e servono invece 16.900 euro. Si tratta di un prezzo promozionale valido per i contratti stipulati entro il 31 dicembre 2026, con uno sconto di 1.000 euro sul prezzo di listino originale di 17.900 euro. Se si vuole puntare sull'allestimento limitato RACE Edition, i prezzi salgono a 16.900 euro per il quadriciclo leggero L6e e toccano i 18.900 euro per la variante MX L7e.

items.title: Libya's top religious authority rules against wearing Nike clothes
items.summary: The US company was named after the Greek goddess of victory, so the Dar al-Ifta said displaying its logo was unIslamic.
items.content:
Libya's highest religious authority, the Dar al-Ifta, has issued a ruling banning Muslims from buying, selling or wearing clothing bearing the Nike logo.

The ruling, issued by the Tripoli-based institution, states that the US sportswear giant was named after the Greek goddess of victory and that its famous swoosh logo was inspired by her wings.

It argued that wearing clothing displaying the logo amounted to promoting symbols associated "with polytheism," or the worship of more than one god.

Libya is home to the ancient Greek city of Cyrene, where archaeological remains include a statue of the Greek goddess of the same name.

The religious committee also accused Nike of supporting Israel and called for a boycott of companies that back the country.

It referred to a statement issued by its Council for Research and Sharia Studies on 5 November 2023, urging Muslims to boycott Western companies it considers supportive of Israel during the war in Gaza.

The ruling, known as a fatwa, is a religious opinion on a matter of Islamic law. It was approved by Libya's Grand Mufti, Sadiq al-Gharyani.

The Dar al-Ifta is an influential religious institution based in Tripoli, in western Libya. The country is politically divided, with rival authorities and institutions operating in the east and west after years of conflict following the toppling of long-time leader Muammar Gaddafi in 2011.

Although its religious rulings can carry considerable social influence, they are not necessarily government orders or legally enforceable.

Last year it ruled against wearing jewellery and watches bearing the logo of French luxury jewellery house Van Cleef & Arpels, arguing that its four-leaf clover design was associated with Christian beliefs and the pursuit of good luck, which it said contradicted Islamic teachings.

The latest fatwa does not announce a state ban on Nike products or specify penalties for people who continue to buy or wear them.

Social media reactions were mixed, with some users welcoming the ruling, while others questioned its significance, describing it as ironic or a distraction from more pressing issues.

The ruling comes amid wider debates over the rise of religious conservatism in public life in Libya.

In 2025, authorities in eastern Libya announced restrictions on rap music, theatre and dance performances, citing concerns that some lyrics and performances violated public morals and Islamic values.

The Dar al-Ifta has also previously issued religious rulings against music, although there is no clear evidence that it was directly involved in the restrictions on performances.

Nike does not operate an official store in Libya, however Nike-branded products are available through local sportswear retailers.

Sportswear brands such as Nike and Adidas are popular across North Africa.

In Libya, as in other countries in the region, counterfeit versions of popular sportswear brands are also sold in local markets.

items.title: Handles are the better pointers (2018)
items.summary: Article URL: https://floooh.github.io/2018/06/17/handles-vs-pointers.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50352767 Points: 15 # Comments: 8
items.content:
28-Nov-2018 : I’ve added a small update at the end on how to prevent ‘handle collisions’ with a per-slot generation counter

…wherein I talk a bit about how I’m doing dynamic memory management in C and C++ these days which basically replaces raw- and smart-pointers with ‘index-handles’.

In my last blog post I was mentioning pointer- and allocation-free programming, but was skipping over the details. This is what the following blog post is about.

This is all based on the (sometimes painful) experience of wrestling for 15+ years with fairly big C++ code bases (0.5 to around 1 mloc) where memory is often managed through smart pointers. The worst case being tens- to hundreds-of-thousands of small C++ objects, each in its own heap allocation, pointing to each other through smart pointers. While such code is quite robust in terms of memory corruption (segfaults and corruption rarely happens, since most attempts are caught by asserts when dereferencing smart pointers), this type of ‘object spiderweb code’ is also dog-slow without obvious starting points for optimization, since the entire code is full of cache misses. Other typical problems are memory fragmentation and ‘fake memory leaks’ because a forgotten smart pointer prevents freeing the underlying memory (I call them ‘fake leaks’ because this type of leaks cannot be caught by memory debugging tools).

Nothing presented here is particularly new or clever, it’s just a collection of a few simple ideas which together work fairly well in bigger code bases to prevent (or at least detect early) a number of common memory-related problems in C and C++, and may even be useful in higher-level garbage-collected languages to reduce pressure on the garbage collector.

However, the underlying design philosophy doesn’t fit very well into a classical OOP world where applications are built from small autonomous objects interacting with each other. That’s why it’s also quite tricky to implement those ideas in a big existing OOP code base, where object creation and destruction happens ‘decentralized’ all over the code.

The approach described here works very well though with a data-oriented architecture, where central systems work on arrays of data items packed tightly in memory.

Most of the following blog post is written from a game developer’s perspective, but should also apply to other areas where a program needs to juggle a few hundred to a few million objects (or generally ‘data items’) in memory, and where such items are created and destroyed frequently.

I’ll explain each of those points in detail below. But the idea is basically that common ‘user-level’ code doesn’t directly call memory allocation functions (like malloc, new or make_shared/make_unique), and reduces the use of pointers to an absolute minimum (only as short-lived references when direct memory access to an item is absolutely needed). Most importantly, pointers are never the ‘owner’ of an item’s underlying memory.

Instead, direct memory manipulation happens as much as possible inside a few centralized systems where memory-related problems are easier to debug and optimize.

In this blog post, a ‘system’ is a (usually fairly big) part of a code base which takes care of a number of related tasks, like ‘rendering’, ‘physics’, ‘AI’, ‘character animation’ and so on. Such a system is separated from other systems and ‘user-code’ through a clearly defined function API, and the work that happens on the system’s data is performed in tight central loops instead of being spread out all over the code base.

Systems often work on items created and destroyed under control of user code (but note that creation and destruction of items is different from allocating and freeing the memory used by those items!). For instance a rendering system might deal with vertex buffers, textures, shaders and pipeline state objects. A physics system works with rigid bodies, joints and collision primitives, and an animation system works with animation keys and curves.

It makes sense to move the memory management for such items into the systems themselves, because a general memory allocator doesn’t have the system-specific ‘domain knowledge’ about how data items are processed and the relationships between data items. This allows the system to optimize memory allocations, perform additional validation checks when creating and destroying items, and arrange items in memory for making best use of the CPU’s data caches.

A good example for this ‘system domain knowledge’ is the destruction of rendering resource objects with modern 3D APIs: a resource object can not simply be destroyed immediately when the user code says so because the resource might still be referenced in a command list waiting to be consumed by the GPU. Instead the rendering system would only mark the resource object for destruction when the user code requests its destruction, but the actual destruction happens at a later time when the GPU no longer uses the resource.

Once all memory management has moved into systems, the system can optimize memory allocations and memory layout with its additional knowledge about how items are used. One obvious optimization is to reduce the number of general memory allocations by grouping items of the same type into arrays, and allocate those arrays at system startup.

Instead of performing a memory allocation each time a new item is created, the system keeps track of free array slots, and picks the next free slot. When the user code no longer needs the item, the system simply marks the slot as free again instead of performing a deallocation (not different from a typical pool allocator).

This pool allocation is most likely a little bit faster than performing a memory allocation per item, but this is not even the main reason for keeping items in arrays (modern general allocators are quite fast too for small allocations).

Keeping system items in arrays instead of unique allocations has the advantage that an item can be identified through an array index instead of requiring a full pointer. This is very useful for memory safety. Instead of handing memory pointers to the outside world, the system can treat the array base pointers as ‘private knowledge’, and only hand out array indices to the public. Without the base pointer to compute an item’s memory location, the outside code can’t access the item’s memory, even with a lot of criminal energy.

If user code needs to access the memory of an item directly it needs to obtain a pointer through a ‘lookup function’ which takes a handle as input and returns a pointer. As soon as such a lookup function exists, the fairly watertight memory safety scenario outlined above is no longer guaranteed, and the user code should adhere to a few rules:

Every time a handle is converted into a pointer, the system can guarantee that the returned pointer still points to the same item that the handle was originally created for (more on this below), but this guarantee ‘decays’ over time since the item under the pointer may have been destroyed, or the underlying memory may have been reallocated to a different location (this is the same problem as iterator invalidation in C++).

The two simple rules above are easy to memorize and are a good compromise between not exposing pointers to user code at all, and having a (somewhat costly) handle-to-pointer conversion for every single memory access.

First, each type of handle should get its own C/C++ type, so that attempting to pass the wrong handle type to a function is already detected at compile time (note that a simple typedef isn’t enough to produce a compiler warning, the handle must be wrapped into its own struct or class - however this could be limited to debug compilation mode).

All runtime memory safety checks happen in the function which converts a handle into a pointer. If the handle is just an array index, it would look like this:

Both can only happen inside one of the system’s functions, that’s why the two ‘pointer usage rules’ exist (don’t store pointers, don’t keep pointers across function calls).

There is a pretty big hole in the above use-after-free check though: if we only check if an array slot behind an index-handle contains a valid item, it’s not guaranteed that it is the same item the handle was originally created for. It can happen that the original item was destroyed, and the same array slot was reused for a new item.

This is where the ‘free bits’ in a handle come in: Let’s say our handles are 16-bits, but we only ever need 1024 items alive at the same time. Only 10 index bits are needed to address 1024 items, which leaves 6 bits free for something else.

If those 6 bits contain some sort of ‘unique pattern’, it’s possible to detect dangling accesses:

This handle-comparison check when converting a handle to a pointer works quite well to detect dangling-accesses, but it isn’t waterproof because the same combination of array index and ‘unique pattern’ will be created sooner or later. But it’s still better than no dangling protection at all (like raw pointers), or a ‘fake memory leak’ which would happen in similar situations with smart pointers.

items.title: Mac at Any Scale
items.summary: Article URL: https://namespace.so/blog/mac-at-any-scale Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50352758 Points: 120 # Comments: 47
items.content:
Chances are you’ve seen me on X : unpacking hundreds of MacBook Pros to deploy in a datacenter. The video hit a nerve: insane enough at the first sight, yet kind of rational if you know what we know now.

So today I want to give some background into what it takes to build custom Mac racks, how we can start macOS instances from scratch in seconds and deliver new Xcode versions mere hours after Apple releases them .

Because our customers need Macs. And because Apple didn’t give us another option.

Many of our customers build and test iOS apps. You can't build iOS apps without a Mac. The iOS Simulator only runs on a Mac. Moreover, in order to release an app to the App Store, Apple requires using a recent Xcode version. xtool xtool is cool, but it is not (yet) a serious replacement. So your coding agent needs a Mac.

But still, why laptops? Isn’t it a major waste of screen pixels and keyboard buttons and battery ions? Well yes, Mac Mini would be a better choice for a datacenter. Sure, it has very rudimentary remote management, no redundant power, and a beautiful case that ensures that cooling will be difficult regardless of which side you lay it on. But these are all known challenges that we have learned to manage.

But have you actually tried to order a couple hundred Minis? We have. Ordered in January, delivered in July. Welcome to the world of 2026 when the supply chains are in disarray. Never mind that Apple doesn’t release updated CPU models to all devices at once. So Mac Mini didn’t get M5 cores for 10 months (and then suddenly got M6 before any other device model!). We promise the best and the newest to our customers so we had to be inventive. That’s how the MacBook-in-Datacenter project was born.

Good design takes iterations; and we surely didn’t get everything right from the first try. But I think we have the system nailed down.

Every MacBook is connected to an IP KVM for remote management. Indispensable when dealing with laptops. Unlike Mac Mini, laptop firmware is designed with the screen in mind: some maintenance actions can only be done by clicking buttons in the beautiful GUI.

Of course, every MacBook gets an external 10G Ethernet NIC. Many folks at Namespace are networking geeks and we are proud of the connection speed and reliability that we provide to customers.

And then there is power. So in total, four cables per laptop, forty-eight per shelf, plus twelve for Ethernet, plus KVM wiring. Let’s just say that careful cable management is essential.

Heat management too. Currently we are deploying custom-made holders, designed to wick the heat from the hotspots and guide hot air away instead of blowing it at the nearby machines.

Naturally, we expected problems and challenges. Just not where they appeared.

I bet some of you looked at the pic above, saw MagSafe cables plugged in and already started writing a snarky tweet that MagSafe is not safe and may get accidentally disconnected.

And yes, I was worried about that too. But the reality is that we have seen very few cases of MagSafe disconnections.

The most unreliable cable? HDMI! Often thick and inflexible. Tends to fall out every time you touch the shelf.

Luckily by now we found almost perfect cables that bend exactly as we want them to bend. And we bought the entire supply of them. There are zero more of them available to order on Amazon.

Another source of pain: FileVault disk encryption. Or rather decryption. When a MacBook reboots (in an unplanned fashion) it prompts for a password to unlock the local disk. The prompt is shown on the screen (of a closed laptop somewhere in the rack, doh). No problem, we thought: we have the KVM connected just for this case!

Nope, not so easy. The password prompt disappears from the external screen after 5 minutes of inactivity. Then we remembered that macOS Tahoe introduced a useful feature: we could unlock FileVault remotely using SSH protocol. Still no luck. On laptops it expires after 5 minutes too. Looks like the only way out of this state is to reboot by physically pressing the button and racing to unlock in time. Mac reboot While on this topic, a small tip: you can reboot a Mac in a way that will keep the disk unlocked when you need it: fdesetup authrestart .

And then there are simply bugs. Under certain conditions, an external USB NIC stops working and acts as if it is not powered and shows no link. Trying another cable, another NIC, another switch port, no luck. But a quick visit to Network Preferences, deleting and recreating the “network service” in MacOS Settings brings it back to life.

At the moment we actually have it easy: M5 and M6 Mac Minis and Studios are coming into our fleet soon. They are way simpler to manage in the DC: they have a built-in 10 Gb network card, they boot up automatically after a power cycle and the OS can be configured entirely automatically via MDM.

But Namespace has some special sauce for the Minis too. We design custom-made shelves that hold the machines with focus on efficient cooling. We have tested a few designs using airflow simulation to arrive at what we are deploying now.

In the end installing Mac Minis is a breeze: unpack them, throw 10 pieces into the holder, connect power and network and press the power button once (famously inconveniently located). From there on automation takes care of them.

Under the hood a Namespace instance is backed by a virtual machine. We have multiple virtual machine engines integrated into a unified platform to run Linux, Windows, and Mac instances in the most efficient way. This way we can provide the same features that make Namespace special, like cache volumes , telemetry, or VPC connections.

Unsurprisingly, our Mac solution is based on Apple’s excellent Virtualization framework . It is an embeddable and flexible virtual machine engine. It’s easiest to compare it to Firecracker in how it fits the system architecture: it implements generic VM operations end-to-end as well as typical peripherals.

For completeness, Apple also provides a lower-level Hypervisor framework , which is comparable to the KVM API of Linux. For instance QEMU uses it on macOS under the hood. Hypervisor provides a way to execute machine code in isolation, but requires the application developer to implement the bulk of machine architecture and peripherals. It could give us a lot of control, but unfortunately it cannot run macOS (it requires an Apple proprietary environment that third parties cannot, or shouldn’t, try to recreate).

In fact, most competing platforms are built on the same foundation. But the details matter: Apple gives us a few primitives that need to be arranged in just the right way to work fast and be secure. The more interesting thing is to watch how different people solve similar problems with different constraints.

A well-known limitation is that Apple only allows two macOS VMs per physical Mac. It can be a Mac Pro with 24 cores and 192 GB memory, yet it is limited to running only two guest VMs. This limitation leaks into our product offering: we can only slice Mac resources in two halves. So we run instances with 6 or 12 cores on 14-core Mac Minis and 8/16-core instances on 18-core MacBooks (we reserve a couple cores for management overhead).

An important consideration of Virtualization VMs is that the virtual CPU is executed by a separate OS process (VMM process in the diagram) from the software integrating Virtualization (here Namespace VM host). If we want to hook some VM behavior or implement custom virtual devices, every interaction with them requires an IPC roundtrip between the VM process and the “host” process. Such context switches are unavoidable and need to be taken into account when designing the system.

Virtualization framework offers a few ways to connect a virtual machine to the network. For instance, bridged and NAT networking modes route traffic directly from the VMM process to the host network interfaces. These are suitable for VMs running on a local computer where the workload is trusted.

Namespace instances run untrusted code and we need to enforce policies on what a VM can or cannot access (these policies can also be customer-defined! ). Also we provide a few additional services to the instances that should appear “as if” they were on the local network for the guest system.

This requires us to take full control of guest networking in the mode where we process every packet that comes out and into the VM in software. We based our guest networking on a userspace TCP/IP stack from Google gVisor project and use it to implement an IP gateway/firewall for the instances. This way we minimize exposure of the host OS to unprocessed packets controlled by the guest.

Network packet handling needs to be very efficient, but as outlined above the path involves IPC. The VMM process needs first to pass the packets to the “VM host” process, which then processes and passes them to the network interface. It takes careful implementation and batch processing wherever possible to minimize the number of IPC roundtrips.
